newsitem.title: FRANCE: Communist set to beat far-rightist in French vote.
newsitem.headline: Communist set to beat far-rightist in French vote.

text.p: A Communist is tipped to beat a far-right candidate on Sunday in a parliamentary by-election that reflects broad misgivings about European integration and frustration with mainstream parties in France.

Communist Roger Mei has the backing of the Socialists and tacit support from the ruling centre-right for a battle against the National Front's Damien Bariller in the southern coal-mining town of Gardanne, where Mei is mayor.
"I think I'll be elected on Sunday, especially since there is a strong movement in this constituency against the candidate of hatred and exclusion," 61-year-old Mei said on Friday.
Bariller, 30 and a rising star in the anti-immigrant party of Jean-Marie Le Pen, says he expects an upset victory after trailing Mei in first round voting last weekend open to all candidates.

Whoever wins, the fight between two candidates opposed to plans for European Union integration including a single currency from 1999 is a blow to mainstream parties in the long run-up to the next legislative elections in 1998.
Parties ranging from Prime Minister Alain Juppe's Gaullist to the Socialists are united in favouring EU integration.

Mei won 37.87 percent last weekend and Bariller 26.80 in the by-election for the National Assembly seat near the southern port of Marseille left open by the resignation of bankrupt businessman and former soccer boss Bernard Tapie.
Tapie's favoured successor, former health and humanitarian action minister Bernard Kouchner also backed by the Socialists, won a dismal 13.29 percent in a vote marred by high abstention.

Parties in the ruling centre-right coalition gave Mei backhanded blessing by giving no recommendations as part of a policy of isolating Le Pen, once described by Juppe as "deeply, almost viscerally racist, anti-Semitic and xenophobic".

"How can one choose between the plague and cholera?" asked Pierre-Andre Wiltzer, spokesman for the centrist Union for French Democracy. Bariller said government parties were effectively pushing for Mei.
Bariller said a judicial probe into Communist leader Robert Hue and other party leaders on suspicion of illegal funding proved the party was "totalitarian and corrupt".
Mei said the probe, announced this week, was part of a political plot to discredit the Communists as a bulwark against the National Front.
